forecaster_note: Peaky, cleanish, fun sized surf at the south-facing spots / N corners today — leftover S swell mixes with a shorter-period NE wind wave for chest-high-or-so peaks. Pretty junky for most spots, but the N corners and more S-facing breaks stay cleanest, especially in the morning. Monday's the day to watch: better looking, head high plus, with winds dropping lighter and maybe going offshore. — Hugh McDowell, Surfline (updated ~21h ago)

wind.summary: NNE 11kph (27kph gusts) already blowing at dawn — offshore at Long Reef, cross-shore at Dee Why and Curl Curl, onshore at Manly. Builds and turns junkier through the morning; Monday looks like the next clean, easing-wind day.

days.label: Today
days.note: Small NNE wind-swell day across the Northern Beaches — Long Reef's offshore angle and FAIR rating make it the standout; Dee Why and Curl Curl are playable early before the cross-shore chop builds; Manly's onshore all day and the softest of the four.

dee-why.window: Best before 9am while the wind stays light — gets choppier as the NNE sea breeze fills in through the morning.
alerts: Secondary swell is near-dead-S (180°) — it wraps badly at the Point, but it's small (2.2ft) so the ENE component is doing the work today

tip.label: Frontside at the Point
tip.text: The 58° ENE component is inside your good window and wraps onto the Point's rights — take it frontside. Size is soft (thigh-stomach) so expect a paddle-heavy session rather than standout waves; the dead-S groundswell underneath is too small to matter much.

long-reef.window: Mid-morning 10am–12pm is prime — offshore NNE holds shape here and it's the best-rated spot on the coast today.

tip.label: Best bet today
tip.text: Offshore wind plus the day's top rating (FAIR) makes Long Reef the standout — worth the drive for the cleanest walls on the Northern Beaches this morning.

curl-curl.window: Early, before the cross-shore chop builds — most consistent (73/100) of the four today.

tip.label: Backside option
tip.text: Cross-shore chop keeps it average, but it's soaking up the dead-S wrap better than Dee Why and has the most energy (105kJ) of the four — backside lefts in the crumble if you don't mind average shape.

manly.window: Onshore all day (27kph gusts) — if you go, first light before the wind wave stacks up further.
alerts: Lowest consistency of the four today (41/100) — onshore chop on small surf

tip.label: Skip unless local
tip.text: Onshore NNE stacking chop on already-small surf, and the softest rating of the four — only worth it if you're already there.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Similar small mixed swell — mostly poor-to-fair through the morning, with Long Reef, Curl Curl and Manly building to a fair window by midday. Dee Why stays the softest of the four.

dee-why.window: A few little peaky waves for the more sheltered spots — pretty junky elsewhere, so keep expectations modest.

long-reef.window: Best-rated spot again tomorrow — fair conditions holding through the late morning.

curl-curl.window: Builds from poor-fair to fair by midday — worth a look around 11am–12pm.

manly.window: Improves toward midday but still the most wind-exposed of the four.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Sat starts small and patchy (poor-to-fair), building into a cleaner 2–3ft NE swell by Sunday. Keep an eye on Monday too — Surfline is calling it a genuinely better day: head-high plus, with winds dropping lighter and maybe swinging offshore.

dee-why.window: Sunday's the pick as the NE swell builds — Saturday is small and inconsistent.

long-reef.window: Best bet of the weekend both days — still the most consistent spot in this swell direction.

curl-curl.window: Sunday's the bigger, more rewarding day here as the NE swell fills in.

manly.window: Stays the softest, most wind-affected option of the weekend.
